policy: Faults ran after the clean matching 5299-test normal baseline; the matching traced suite also passed 5299 tests.

Counter/invariant witnesses are not claimed as stronger GC or wait-only proofs. Each row retains its actual caller and witness scope.
Diagnostic excerpts may be truncated at 4000 characters; exact full-diagnostic and raw report hashes identify the retained temporary evidence. Tests and fault edits are pinned and reproducible.

The fault removes Set deletion after settlement, distinct from the existing fault that unregisters too early.

reconciliationResolutions.resolution: The new fault preserves completed reject actions in a live execution and is detected by exact result-Promise/result-value GC after fulfillment and rejection, with live-output and still-pending fatal-delivery controls. Existing outward-registration-lasts-until-settlement remains the opposite timing direction.

obligations.witnessScope: Distinct work fixtures cover exclusive point mutation, bounded candidate allocation, independent fork notification and iterative entry history. They do not establish the B22 aggregate bound by themselves.

obligations.obligation: Authorized canonical publication does not depend on a cache length already matching logical bounds
obligations.callers: ArrayView placementDestination -> canonical producer mutationTarget; delayed creation followed by pop and entry write
obligations.witnessScope: The program 1948 public reduction and four delivery controls exercise a logically in-range slot while physical backing remains empty. The fault restores the old bounded-view guard and must fail the intended native/rejected cases. obligations.obligation: Existing nested preparation and delivered-question bookkeeping avoid completed history
obligations.callers: placement-structure shared prepare identity; array-length question delivery release
obligations.witnessScope: entry-history-work counts the nested preparation path separately from B22 append counts; the open-owner length-question test checks immediate registration removal. Neither result replaces the aggregate no-history producer bound.

obligations.obligation: Canonical index retirement releases obsolete owners while backing and producer stay live
obligations.callers: retireRelationships canonical backingCounterVersions/counterProjections cleanup
obligations.witnessScope: Exact new-loop fault has both immediate reciprocal-membership/late-settlement assertions and a child GC oracle for a retired indexed view with live out-of-range backing owner. This is independent of owner override membership detachment and physical backing-owner registration cleanup.

obligations.obligation: Backing producer construction owns no unused logical length or diagnostic source history
obligations.callers: ArrayBackingProducers stores only backing/start coordinates; required physical length/extension/population boundaries clear source bindings
obligations.witnessScope: Restoring the redundant constructor length read reintroduces a swept supported failure and lazy-stack retention. Separate faults remove required physical-read cleanup, synchronous extension cleanup, or prepared suffix cleanup. These preserve required reflection failures and exact poison diagnostics rather than suppressing errors.

sourceReasoning: For the no-retained-output scalar target there are N canonical versions, N logical outgoing records, N+1 physical slots and constant live holder/owner entries; new views retire normally. No per-view producer list or forwarding history replaces removed overlay captures.

Shared producer records keep one current version per physical index. Local override history stays in ordinary current placements/captures; there is no eager per-slot reclamation scan or new interval index.

The strict snapshot enumerates every maintained store on the target history live root/current view/raw backing/two records, including reciprocal optional memberships. This is not a claim to count every JavaScript allocation for arbitrary output graphs.

ArrayView.backingVersions bounds metadata enumeration by min(selected index span, maintained producer entries), applies offsets and local masks, and performs no host inspection. Physical candidate enumeration on shorter retained native owners stays range-bounded.
limitations: The complete scalar-history bound requires the counter witness plus writer/release audit; a single removed guard cannot establish all possible hidden allocations. This is a whole-cost proof obligation, not a reason to mark an injectable semantic guard unsuitable.
Requested historical outputs, retained views and indexed graph data have explicit output/dependency costs and are separate controls, not exempted failures in the no-history target.
